answers.otherText:
Consultation response: REVISE_SOURCE — one P2 finding (F1) on exact be242236534f05fbf4ef895db85a780f8d6e1716, tree 515945c2fa280060b7ace4bbbdfccbfbc8d25a47, base ed78cd5.

F1 — the shared RPC deadline does not bound HTTP header reads. At vanguard/network/profile-integration.py:124–125, remaining() sets a socket timeout once before HTTPConnection.getresponse(). CPython getresponse() calls HTTPResponse.begin(), which reads status/header lines internally. Its timeout bounds idle socket reads; periodic input resets that wait without returning to remaining(). The same issue can affect internal chunk framing. The final timeout eventually reports failure, but only after the peer stops progressing. The intended five-second absolute call budget, and a shorter remaining driver budget, are therefore not enforced throughout this blocking operation.

Independent real loopback reproduction on the exact candidate, with no native/Docker/admission effects:

- Keep driver.DEADLINE 60 seconds away. Accept the POST on a disposable 127.0.0.1 socket; send HTTP/1.1 200 OK, then eight harmless header lines 0.75 seconds apart, then Content-Length: 2 and {}. RPC.call waits 6.0018 seconds on Python 3.15.2 and 6.0015 seconds on Python 3.12.3 before TimeoutError, exceeding the unchanged five-second call budget. Every gap is below the socket timeout. More progressing header input can extend that wait further.
- With driver.DEADLINE only 0.12 seconds away and eight header lines 0.05 seconds apart, the same call returns ValueError after 0.4078/0.4054 seconds. Thus this is also observable against the existing driver deadline, rather than only a mocked clock.
- The new delayed-response test at test_direct_profile.py:210–216 tests silence before the first response. The budget test at :224–248 substitutes getresponse(); neither exercises progressing HTTP headers.

Smallest correction: enforce the same existing absolute end while status/header/body-framing reads are blocked, then close the owned socket/response on expiry. Keep one connection and at most one Digest response, stdlib Digest generation, all existing budgets and fixed public diagnostics. Add connected progressing-header controls on the unauthenticated challenge and authenticated response, plus applicable chunk-framing/error closure, with a normal successful session control. The current candidate must fail the deadline controls; the correction must exit near the original deadline without leaked work. Do not extend timeouts or alter native predicates. P2P owns this ordinary bounded source correction and refreeze; a second failed round on F1 returns to the lead. This finding does not establish a breach of the outer controller's separately enforced phase/container limits.

Cleared within this source scope: all 84 guarded direct tests pass independently on Python 3.15.2, zero failures/errors/skips, 14.955s, ResourceWarning as error. They include exact ed78cd5 refusal on session-nonce authentication, candidate daemon snapshot/raw401, wallet get_balance/all17 -7 schemas, rotated credentials, stale/closed/unsupported challenge handling, closure and export controls. These are disposable server/substituted-native observations, not real restricted-handler acceptance. The per-connection nonce fixture agrees with pinned e151643c's http_custom_handler.m_auth ownership and nonce/nc checks. The authentication correction itself works in those controls.

Authenticated packet b62bd3cd matches 2004584 bytes/SHA256 d77e92dc08dfe8ad2be02c634c57bb64a4155c83d78c08afa4d2223c1101e57e; separate manifest 63fd1117 matches 49069 bytes/SHA256 5b46f284fc6f119e76ce00da4465fda6eac0f8063e09459ca0c7cbd578be6eb9. All290 members including manifest verify; 100 candidate/100 baseline/23 evidence Git snapshots and current bytes match. All67 candidate/32 reference input bindings verify; non-candidate inputs and actual build_identity are unchanged. The two relevant upstream auth snapshots match exact pinned Git objects; the other63 upstream snapshots were content-hash checked. Runner/inputs bindings match the request. Source outside RPC.call, dependent anchors/tests/bindings remains preserved. Zero original-lock touches; tracked source unchanged and existing unowned bytecode preserved.

Reviewer script and raw results are in this run's deadline-probe.py, deadline-python315.jsonl, deadline-python312.jsonl and platform-direct.log; source-verification.json records bindings.
